words.definition: the movement of respiratory gases between an organism and its environment or internal transport system
words.example: Gas exchange supplies oxygen and removes carbon dioxide in many animals.

words.definition: a specialized surface across which respiratory gases diffuse
words.example: Alveoli form the gas exchange surface in human lungs.

words.definition: a difference in concentration or partial pressure that drives net diffusion
words.example: Ventilation and blood flow maintain a steep diffusion gradient for oxygen in the lungs.

words.definition: a tiny air sac in the lung where gas exchange occurs
words.example: Oxygen diffuses from an alveolus into surrounding capillaries.

words.definition: the thin internal lung surface formed by alveoli and specialized for gas exchange
words.example: The alveolar surface is moist, thin and extensive.

words.definition: a substance that reduces surface tension at an interface
words.example: Lung surfactant reduces surface tension and helps prevent alveoli from collapsing.

words.definition: a small airway that branches from bronchi and leads toward alveoli
words.example: Bronchioles regulate airflow to different regions of the lung.

words.definition: a dense arrangement of tiny blood vessels supplying a tissue or exchange surface
words.example: A rich capillary network maintains blood flow around alveoli.

words.definition: movement of air or water across a gas exchange surface
words.example: Ventilation continually refreshes air in the lungs.

words.definition: a sheet of muscle below the lungs that changes thoracic volume during breathing
words.example: Contraction of the diaphragm increases thoracic volume during inhalation.

words.definition: a muscle between ribs that helps move the rib cage during breathing
words.example: External intercostal muscles help lift the ribs during inhalation.

words.definition: movement of air into the lungs
words.example: During inhalation, thoracic volume increases and air pressure in the lungs falls.

words.definition: movement of air out of the lungs
words.example: During quiet exhalation, elastic recoil helps reduce lung volume.

words.definition: the volume of air moved into or out of the lungs in one normal breath
words.example: Tidal volume increases during exercise.

words.definition: the maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after a maximal inhalation
words.example: Vital capacity can be estimated with spirometry.

words.definition: the additional volume of air that can be inhaled after a normal inhalation
words.example: Inspiratory reserve volume contributes to vital capacity.

words.definition: the additional volume of air that can be exhaled after a normal exhalation
words.example: Expiratory reserve volume is measured during forced breathing.

words.definition: a microscopic pore in the epidermis of a leaf or stem that allows gas exchange
words.example: Carbon dioxide enters a leaf through a stoma.

words.definition: a specialized epidermal cell that changes shape to control opening of a stoma
words.example: Guard cells regulate stomatal opening and water loss.

words.definition: loss of water vapour from plant aerial surfaces, mainly through stomata
words.example: Transpiration can increase when stomata are open in dry air.

words.definition: a very small blood vessel with a thin wall specialized for exchange between blood and tissues
words.example: Capillaries allow short diffusion distances between blood and cells.

words.definition: a blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart under relatively high pressure
words.example: Arteries have thick muscular and elastic walls.

words.definition: a blood vessel that carries blood toward the heart at relatively low pressure
words.example: Many veins contain valves that prevent backflow.

words.definition: the internal space within a tubular structure such as a blood vessel
words.example: Veins generally have a wider lumen than comparable arteries.

words.definition: the layered wall of an artery, adapted to withstand and maintain high blood pressure
words.example: Elastic tissue in the arterial wall stretches during systole.

words.definition: a flap-like structure in a vein that prevents reverse flow of blood
words.example: Venous valves help return blood from the legs to the heart.

words.definition: the rhythmic expansion of arteries caused by pressure waves from heart contractions
words.example: Pulse rate usually rises during exercise.

words.definition: the force exerted by blood against the walls of blood vessels
words.example: Arterial blood pressure is highest close to the heart.

words.definition: an artery that supplies oxygenated blood to heart muscle
words.example: A blocked coronary artery can reduce oxygen supply to the myocardium.

words.definition: disease caused by reduced blood flow through coronary arteries, often because of atherosclerotic narrowing
words.example: Coronary heart disease can increase the risk of myocardial infarction.

words.definition: partial or complete blockage of a vessel or passage
words.example: An occlusion in a coronary artery can interrupt blood flow to heart tissue.

words.definition: plant vascular tissue that transports water and mineral ions mainly from roots to shoots
words.example: Water moves upward through xylem in the transpiration stream.

words.definition: a long hollow tube formed from dead lignified cells that conducts water in vascular plants
words.example: Xylem vessels provide low-resistance pathways for water transport.

words.definition: the continuous movement of water from roots through xylem to leaves and the atmosphere
words.example: The transpiration stream carries mineral ions toward leaves.

words.definition: tension generated in xylem when evaporation from leaves draws water upward
words.example: Transpiration pull helps lift water through tall plants.

words.definition: the mechanism in which cohesion between water molecules allows tension generated by transpiration to pull a continuous water column through xylem
words.example: The cohesion-tension mechanism explains passive water transport in xylem.

words.definition: a strong hydrophobic polymer deposited in some plant cell walls
words.example: Lignin strengthens xylem vessel walls and prevents collapse under tension.

words.definition: a thin region in a lignified cell wall that permits lateral movement of water between xylem cells
words.example: Water can move between adjacent xylem vessels through pits.

words.definition: a strand of transport tissue containing xylem and phloem
words.example: Vascular bundles run through stems and leaf veins.

words.definition: the outer cell layer of a root, involved in absorption from the soil
words.example: Root epidermal cells can form root hairs that increase absorptive surface area.

words.definition: the tissue region between the epidermis and vascular tissue in a root or stem
words.example: Water can move across the root cortex toward the xylem.
